Section 1 of 14

Is History Going Anywhere?

The future can feel uncertain.

Wars continue. The cost of living rises. Families experience loss. Leaders make promises they cannot keep. Technology changes faster than people can adjust. Many young adults wonder whether life will become safer, more just, or more meaningful.

The Bible says history is moving toward a real event.

Jesus will return.

His return will not be an idea, private vision, or hidden spiritual experience. He will personally come back to Earth with power and glory.

He is returning to end the rule of sin, raise His people from the dead, gather those who trust Him, and bring them home.

The future is not in the hands of human governments, corporations, armies, or technology. It is in the hands of the Creator.

Jesus Promised to Return

Read John 14:1–3 ↗.

On the night before His death, Jesus knew His followers were about to experience grief and confusion. He gave them a promise:

He was going away, preparing a place for them, and coming back.

Jesus did not say, “You may find your way to Me.”

He said, “I will come again.”

The same Jesus who healed the sick, welcomed outsiders, gave His life on the cross, and rose from the dead will return.

His promise is personal. He wants His people to be where He is.

Why Has He Waited So Long?

Nearly two thousand years have passed since Jesus promised to return. Why has He not come yet?

Read 2 Peter 3:8–9 ↗.

The Creator experiences time differently from us. What feels like a long delay does not mean He has forgotten His promise.

He waits because He is patient. He wants people to have an opportunity to turn toward Him and receive life.

Every additional day is evidence of mercy.

The Creator is not waiting because He approves of suffering. He is allowing the conflict between good and evil to reach its full conclusion while inviting as many people as possible to be saved.

Read Matthew 24:14 ↗.

God’s message will reach every nation before the end comes. He wants people everywhere to hear the truth about His character and make a free choice.

How Will Jesus Return?

The Bible gives clear details so that we do not have to guess.

His return will be personal

Read Acts 1:9–11 ↗.

After speaking with His followers, Jesus rose into the sky. Angels told them that the same Jesus would return in the same way they had seen Him leave.

Jesus will not send a substitute. He will return personally.

His return will be visible

Read Revelation 1:7 ↗.

Every eye will see Him.

Read Matthew 24:27 ↗.

Jesus compared His coming to lightning that flashes across the sky. It will not be limited to one building, city, reservation, nation, or part of the world.

His return cannot be hidden by a government or controlled by a religious institution.

His return will be heard

Read 1 Thessalonians 4:16–17 ↗.

Jesus will descend with a commanding shout, the voice of the archangel, and the trumpet of God.

The Bible does not describe His return as silent or secret.

It will be the greatest public event in human history.

His return will be glorious

Read Matthew 25:31 ↗.

Jesus will come in His glory with all the angels.

Read Matthew 24:30–31 ↗.

The nations of Earth will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds with power and great glory. His angels will gather His people from every direction.

No human event can compare with it.

Will Jesus Return Secretly?

Some people teach that Jesus will secretly remove His followers while everyone else continues with life as usual.

The Bible describes something much larger.

Every eye will see Him.

A trumpet will sound.

The heavens will be filled with angels.

The dead who trusted Jesus will rise.

The living followers of Jesus will be gathered with them.

People who rejected Him will recognize what is happening.

Jesus compared His return to lightning because it will be unmistakable.

Read Matthew 24:23–27 ↗.

Jesus warned that people would claim He had appeared in a private room, distant location, or hidden place.

He said not to believe those reports.

You will not need someone to send you a link, reveal a secret location, or convince you that Jesus has returned. When the real Jesus comes, the entire world will know.

What Happens to Those Who Died Trusting Jesus?

Read 1 Thessalonians 4:13–18 ↗.

The Bible describes those who have died trusting Jesus as sleeping. Death is real, but it is not permanent.

When Jesus returns, He will call them from their graves.

The righteous dead will rise with new, immortal bodies. Their first sight will be the face of their Creator and Friend.

Those who are alive and faithful when Jesus returns will be changed.

Read 1 Corinthians 15:51–54 ↗.

Mortal bodies will become immortal. Bodies damaged by age, illness, injury, disability, or disease will be made whole.

Death will lose its power.

Families Will Be Reunited

Many families carry empty places.

Someone died too young. A child never came home. A grandparent passed before important questions could be asked. A friend’s life ended without enough time to say goodbye.

The return of Jesus brings the promise of reunion.

Read Isaiah 25:8–9 ↗.

The Creator will swallow up death and wipe away tears.

When Jesus returns, graves will open. Those who trusted Him will live again. The separation caused by death will end.

This hope does not remove today’s grief. Jesus understands mourning and gives us permission to grieve.

Read John 11:33–36 ↗.

Jesus wept at the grave of His friend Lazarus, even though He knew resurrection was coming.

Hope and grief can exist together.

Who Will Be Gathered?

Read Revelation 7:9–10 ↗.

John saw a great crowd that no one could count. They came from every nation, tribe, people, and language.

God’s final family is not limited to one race, culture, country, or social class.

Native people will be there.

People from Africa, Asia, Europe, the Pacific, the Arctic, the Caribbean, and every part of the Americas will be there.

Their presence before God is not described as a gathering of people whose identities have been erased. John still recognizes nations, tribes, peoples, and languages.

The Creator creates unity without making everyone culturally identical.

Everyone is united by loyalty to Jesus. No group stands above another. No one has a better place because of ancestry, wealth, education, or social position.

Read Galatians 3:26–29 ↗.

All who belong to Jesus receive the same promise and stand before the Creator with equal value.

Does Belonging to God Mean Losing Your Native Identity?

The Creator’s plan is restoration, not cultural disappearance.

Sin has damaged every culture. It has also led powerful groups to dominate, exploit, or erase others.

Jesus removes sin, pride, hatred, idolatry, injustice, and everything that separates people from God. He does not remove the human dignity, relationships, creativity, and distinct identity He designed people to have.

Read Revelation 21:24–26 ↗.

The nations bring their honor into the restored city. Whatever is beautiful, truthful, and good finds its place under the Creator’s authority.

Your place in God’s family does not depend on becoming like another race.

It depends on belonging to Jesus.

What Will Happen to Injustice?

Human justice is often incomplete.

Some people never admit what they did. Some institutions never return what they took. Some victims die without seeing accountability. Some crimes are forgotten by everyone except those who still carry the pain.

The Creator has not forgotten.

Read Ecclesiastes 12:13–14 ↗.

God sees every hidden action.

Read Revelation 22:12 ↗.

When Jesus returns, He brings His reward with Him.

His judgment is completely informed and completely fair. He cannot be bribed, deceived, pressured, or influenced by status.

The return of Jesus means that injustice will not continue forever.

The Creator will defend truth, rescue His people, and bring the conflict with evil toward its final end.

How Will People Respond When Jesus Appears?

Not everyone will welcome His return.

Read Revelation 6:14–17 ↗.

Those who continually rejected the Creator and chose rebellion will be terrified by the presence of Jesus.

They are not afraid because Jesus suddenly became cruel. They are afraid because they spent their lives resisting His truth and refusing His mercy.

Those who trust Jesus will respond differently.

Read Isaiah 25:9 ↗.

They will say, “This is our God. We have waited for Him, and He will save us.”

The same event produces two responses.

One group hides from Jesus.

The other welcomes Him.

The difference is the relationship each person chose before He came.

Can Someone Pretend to Be Jesus?

Read 2 Corinthians 11:14 ↗.

Satan can present himself as an angel of light. Before the true return of Jesus, powerful spiritual deceptions will take place.

A being may appear impressive, speak kindly, perform signs, or claim to bring peace. Supernatural power alone does not prove that someone comes from the Creator.

Remember the biblical signs of Jesus’ return:

  • Jesus comes in the sky.
  • Every eye sees Him.
  • All the angels come with Him.
  • A great trumpet is heard.
  • The righteous dead rise.
  • God’s people are gathered from across the world.

Jesus does not quietly walk around Earth before these things happen.

Do not leave to meet someone claiming to be Jesus at a special location. Do not accept a spiritual being simply because the experience feels powerful.

Test every claim by Scripture.

Can We Know the Date?

Read Matthew 24:36 ↗.

Jesus said no human being knows the day or hour of His return.

Anyone who announces an exact date is claiming knowledge Jesus said people do not possess.

The Bible gives signs that show His coming is near. We will study those signs in the next lesson.

Signs help us recognize the season. They do not give us permission to set a date.

The Creator wants us to live ready every day rather than become excited by predictions for a few weeks.

What Does It Mean to Be Ready?

Being ready does not mean living in constant fear.

It does not mean becoming obsessed with disasters, rumors, politics, or every alarming video posted online.

Read John 15:4–10 ↗.

Readiness means remaining connected to Jesus.

A person preparing for His return:

  • Trusts Jesus for forgiveness
  • Listens to the Holy Spirit
  • Studies Scripture
  • Follows the Creator’s commands
  • Makes wrongs right when possible
  • Treats people with dignity
  • Resists deception
  • Uses personal gifts to serve others
  • Shares hope without using pressure
  • Continues growing in love and truth

You are not ready because you have reached perfection through your own effort.

You are ready because you belong to Jesus and continue walking with Him.

What If You Feel Afraid of the Second Coming?

Some people first heard about the end of the world through frightening sermons, disturbing images, or threats.

Fear may gain attention for a moment, but the Creator wants more than a frightened response.

Read 1 John 4:17–19 ↗.

Love gives us confidence and drives out fear.

If Jesus is your Creator, Savior, and Friend, His return is not the arrival of a stranger. It is the return of the One who gave His life for you.

Imagine someone you deeply trust coming to take you away from a dangerous place and bring you home.

That is the hope of the Second Coming.

Why Does This Promise Matter Today?

The promise of Jesus’ return changes how we live now.

Because He is returning, suffering is temporary.

Because He is returning, death will not have the last word.

Because He is returning, hidden injustice will be judged.

Because He is returning, faithfulness matters even when no one notices.

Because He is returning, your future does not depend on the stability of this world.

Because He is returning, hope is stronger than fear.

Read Titus 2:11–14 ↗.

Waiting for Jesus is active. His grace teaches us how to live with self-control, honesty, faithfulness, and purpose today.

Who Should Hear This Hope?

Read Revelation 14:6–7 ↗.

God’s final message goes to every nation, tribe, language, and people.

No one should be pressured, manipulated, or treated as a project. The Creator respects human freedom, and His followers should do the same.

You can share hope by:

  • Listening before speaking
  • Treating questions with respect
  • Acknowledging when religious people have caused harm
  • Explaining what Scripture actually teaches
  • Living in a way that reflects Jesus
  • Offering an invitation without trying to control the response

The message belongs to the Creator. Our responsibility is to share it truthfully and lovingly.

Think About It

Write your answers in your own words.

  1. What feelings arise when you think about Jesus returning?
  2. Which promise about His return gives you the most hope?
  3. What details show that the Second Coming will not be secret?
  4. Is there someone you hope to see in the resurrection?
  5. What does Revelation 7 ↗ show about identity in the Creator’s family?
  6. Why does Jesus wait before returning?
  7. How can you test someone who claims to be Jesus?
  8. What is the difference between watching for Jesus and becoming controlled by fear?
  9. What part of your life would change if you believed Jesus could return soon?
  10. Who could you encourage with the promise of resurrection and reunion?

Try This During the Coming Week

Set aside fifteen quiet minutes each day.

Read one passage:

  • Day 1: John 14:1–3 ↗
  • Day 2: Acts 1:6–11 ↗
  • Day 3: Matthew 24:23–31 ↗
  • Day 4: 1 Thessalonians 4:13–18 ↗
  • Day 5: 1 Corinthians 15:50–55 ↗
  • Day 6: Revelation 7:9–17 ↗
  • Day 7: Isaiah 25:6–9 ↗

After each reading, write down:

  • What will happen when Jesus returns?
  • What promise gives me hope?
  • What warning should I remember?
  • How can this truth affect the way I live today?

Choose one person who is grieving, anxious about the future, or feeling discouraged. Share one promise from these passages in a gentle and personal way.

A Prayer You Can Pray

Creator God, thank You for promising that Jesus will return. When the future feels uncertain, help me remember that history remains in Your hands. Prepare my heart without allowing fear to control me. Keep me close to Jesus and protect me from spiritual deception. Comfort everyone who is grieving and help us trust Your promise of resurrection and reunion. Thank You for gathering people from every nation, tribe, and language without erasing who they are. Help me live faithfully and share this hope with respect and love. Amen.

Remember This

Jesus personally promised to return.

His coming will be visible, audible, worldwide, and glorious.

The Second Coming will not be silent or secret.

The righteous dead will rise, and the faithful living will be transformed.

The Creator will gather people from every nation, tribe, people, and language.

Belonging to God does not require cultural erasure.

No one knows the exact day or hour of Jesus’ return.

Powerful spiritual experiences must be tested by Scripture.

Readiness means remaining in a saving relationship with Jesus.

For those who trust Him, the Second Coming is a promise of rescue, resurrection, reunion, justice, and home.

Coming Next

Jesus told His followers that certain conditions would appear before His return. The next lesson examines those signs and explains how to watch with wisdom, peace, and hope.
